doc:
The machine-readable description of what the library can do. It is pure data with no file behind it, identical in every binding, so it needs no test data and covers a lot of surface for its size: if a category or a parameter goes missing in one binding, it shows up here rather than in whatever feature happened to use it.

These cases deliberately do NOT pin the length of the registry blob. Every feature that registers something moves it, so a byte count turns each unrelated addition into a red conformance run -- and it is not a cross-language claim anyway, since all four would move together. What is pinned is the category list and the entries each category must contain, which is what a binding could actually get wrong.

cases.doc: The categories, in the order the registry lists them.
The whole registry, checked for the keys it must contain. The blob's length is deliberately not pinned -- see the area note.
One category on its own, which is the call a binding actually makes.
Asking for a category that does not exist answers rather than throws -- a caller enumerating categories should not have to guard every call.
